the imaginary potential based on high-energy interactions in nuclear matter, with system and energy dependent normalization, is a universal potential that describes well the data for a wide range of heavy-ion reactions.

we present new coupled-channel calculations with the Sao-Paulo potential (SPP), as the bare interaction and an imaginary potential, with system and energy-independent normalization, that has been developed in order to take into account dissipation processes in heavy-ion collisions.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dissipative processes in reactions of heavy ions, using the Sao Paulo Potential as the bare interaction.

the development and implementation of an imaginary potential with energy and system-independent normalization for dissipative reactions, and its application to heavy-ion reactions at energies above the Coulomb barrier.

the development of a new imaginary potential with universal system and energy independent norm that has been successfully used in the description of dissipative effects in heavy ion collisions at intermediate energies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SPP with the imaginary potential developed in the present work provides a universal normalization for heavy-ion reactions in the energy region of 20–100 MeV/nucleon.
the new imaginary potential, with a system independent normalization factor, is very promising and can be used for a wide range of heavy-ion reactions.

the new SPP + imaginary potential is able to reproduce the experimental data for a wide range of systems, energies, and mass numbers, and therefore it is an excellent candidate to be used as an alternative for the standard Woods–Saxon potential in the description of heavy-ion reactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SPP with an imaginary potential of system and energy independent strength is a very good approximation for heavy-ion collisions.
this imaginary potential with universal norm is a very good choice to describe dissipative processes in the whole energy range of interest.
this new model is able to reproduce the experimental cross sections for the elastic scattering, total reaction and total inelastic channels in a large energy range.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a system and energy independent imaginary potential with a universal normalization, that is independent on the type of the reaction, is able to reproduce experimental data with very good accuracy.
the imaginary potential is universal for dissipative processes and can be applied in a broad range of energies and systems.
the SPP, with an energy independent normalization of the imaginary potential, is a universal bare interaction for the description of the elastic and inelastic scattering of heavy ions.
